full_judgment: 3. According to the plaintiff's case, as made out in the plaint, the disputed lends appertained to the Estate of Bishweshwar Roy Choudhury, which were diluviated and after the said lands had reappeared as reformation in stu and had become fit for possession. Babu Rajeswar Choudhury, the then executor of the -10/- annas share of the Estate of late Bishweshwar Roy Choudhury settled the said lands with the predecessors of plaintiffs 1 to 42 and plaintiff No. 45 at an annual rent of Tk. 250/- on the basis of a Karsha Kabuliyat dated 1st Jaistha, 1331 B.S. corresponding to May, 1924.  The proprietors of 6/- annas share of the said Estate settled their 6/- annas share of the said lands with some of the defendants at an annual rent of 7k. 75/- on the basis of another Kabuliyat of the sane date, namely, 1st Jaistha, 1331 B.S. which were ultimately sold, and purchased in auction by the landlords, in execution of a decree for rent obtained by them and were then settled in 1344-45 13.S. with the predecessors of some of the plaintiffs on the basis of a Kabuliyat at a rental of Tk. 75. After the rent receiving interests of the previous landlords had been acquired under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 the Government has stepped into the shoes of the previous landlords and the plaintiffs have become tenants directly under the Government, in respect of the said lands, some of which had been wrongly recorded in the name of the Government. The Government, however, have had no right, title and interest in the said lands nor any right to dispossess the plaintiffs from any part thereof, which are the lands of their tenancy.
